speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for Health in light of the first case of Zika virus infection in Singapore (a) whether the Ministry will issue travel alerts for Singaporeans who are visiting countries which are considered as high risk; and (b) whether there will be a multi-Ministry effort to look into the control and management of infectious disease outbreaks, given Singapore's high tourism traffic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We advised travellers who have returned to Singapore from affected areas to monitor their health and consult a doctor if they have symptoms of Zika, such as fever, skin rashes, joint and muscle pains, headaches and red eyes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH also informed hospitals and doctors about the notification, testing and clinical management for suspected Zika cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: If they have to travel to these areas, they should take strict precautions to protect themselves against mosquito bites.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This approach has been effective in dealing with previous global outbreaks, such as the 2014 Ebola outbreak in West Africa and the 2015 MERS outbreak in the Middle East and the Republic of Korea.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: With the Rio Olympics next month, we are a bit concerned whether the Zika virus will be brought back to the region by those who are participating in the Olympics or just going to attend the Olympics.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What control measures do we now have to protect our athletes, as well as to make sure that when they come back, whether they will be screened to see if they have the Zika virus?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: My concern is that we do have the vector here.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Once the Zika virus sets root in Singapore, it is very hard to get rid 	Page: 31 of it.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The other supplementary question is whether there is any regional platform, for example, coordinating with our Malaysian and Indonesian counterparts, on the battle against Zika.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Once it gets into the region, Singapore will not be spared.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On his first question, we have travellers from all over the world.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With the Rio Olympics, because Brazil is one of the affected countries, there will be people who will be travelling to Brazil and then, subsequently, travelling to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is also people who attend the Olympics in Brazil.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, when they are in Brazil, to protect themselves against mosquito bites, they should be wearing clothing that will cover the body, arms and legs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They should apply insect repellent and also take precautions to sleep in air-conditioned rooms or under mosquito nets to keep out the mosquitoes.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And, very importantly, also to monitor for symptoms.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These advisories that we provide are not just for the athletes and officials but all travellers who are visiting countries experiencing Zika outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second question that the Member asked is with regard to regional cooperation.
